meta.scope: Bolivia batch 4 — Fiscal depth (budget, tax collection, public debt, YPFB), labour informality as lived structure, and additional departments (Cochabamba, Tarija, Oruro, Beni). Continues the thorough lived-economy picture.

candidates.title: Presupuesto General del Estado / National Budget
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas Públicas
candidates.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the public sector.
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links tax, hydrocarbon (IDH, royalties) and other revenues with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment. Recent budgets reflect pressure from declining gas income and rising debt service.

candidates.title: Recaudación tributaria y aduanera
candidates.description: Tax and customs collection statistics. Primary non-hydrocarbon revenue-side fiscal product.
candidates.notes: Core revenue statistic. Complements the declining IDH/royalty stream. Large stocks of uncollected tax debt have become a policy issue.

candidates.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
candidates.description: Stock and flow statistics of public debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator under fiscal pressure.
candidates.notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Domestic debt has grown sharply as external financing tightened and deficits persisted; recent fiscal deficits have been in the double-digit % of GDP range.

candidates.title: Yacimientos Petrolíferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB)
candidates.description: State hydrocarbons company. Producer, exporter and fiscal contributor (royalties, IDH) of natural gas and related products.
candidates.notes: Institutional parent of the gas-era fiscal model. Production and export decline has cascading effects on IDH, royalties, YPFB finances and the broader public-sector accounts.

candidates.title: Informalidad laboral / Labour informality
candidates.description: Share of employed persons in informal employment. Structural feature of the Bolivian labour market and a primary determinant of household income security.
candidates.notes: Lived-economy cornerstone. Informality rates are among the highest in South America (often cited near or above 80% of employment). Most households depend primarily or exclusively on informal income; formal employment is strongly protective against poverty.

candidates.title: Departamento de Cochabamba — central valley hub
candidates.description: Central valley department and the third major population and economic pole after La Paz and Santa Cruz. Intermediate poverty and large absolute poverty mass.
candidates.notes: Completes the central economic axis (La Paz–Cochabamba–Santa Cruz). Large absolute number of people in poverty even when rates are not the highest.

candidates.title: Departamento de Tarija — southern gas and agricultural zone
candidates.description: Southern department historically linked to gas production and agricultural activity. Intermediate poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: Gas-producing department. Poverty rates intermediate; economic structure has been shaped by the hydrocarbon cycle that is now contracting.

candidates.title: Departamento de Oruro — highland mining
candidates.description: Highland mining department with intermediate-to-elevated poverty.
candidates.notes: Mining geography. Completes the highland departmental set alongside Potosí, Chuquisaca and La Paz.

candidates.title: Departamento del Beni — northern lowland
candidates.description: Northern Amazonian lowland department. Intermediate poverty with marked urban–rural gaps.
candidates.notes: Lowland contrast to the highland departments. Completes the geographic coverage of the main departmental poverty gradient.

candidates.title: Empresas públicas — performance and fiscal exposure
candidates.description: State-owned enterprise sector (YPFB, YLB, BoA, Mi Teleférico, Mutún, etc.). Material source of fiscal risk when losses and debt accumulate.
candidates.notes: Lived fiscal-risk node. A large group of state firms have operated at a loss; a subset has been flagged as critically indebted. Restructuring and possible liquidation have entered the policy agenda as gas rents decline.

proposed_edges.basis: IDH and hydrocarbon royalties remain material revenue lines in the national budget.
Tax and customs collection are core components of budgeted revenues.
Public-debt dynamics are inseparable from the financing of the national budget.
YPFB is the institutional producer and exporter of natural gas.
IDH and royalty flows originate from YPFB hydrocarbon operations.
Informality rates are derived from the household-survey employment modules.
Informal workers face substantially higher poverty incidence than formal workers.
Cochabamba’s poverty ranking and absolute poverty mass are derived from the departmental tables.
SOE losses and debt create contingent fiscal claims on the national budget.
